facts.text: The fall is operational. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.

Each gap states what is missing, what it restricts, its severity and the action that would close it.

The issuer-adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 is printed in no supplied source, so the six adjusted ratio rows for FY2024 and the FY2024 adjusted EBITDA cell are not supplied; this restricts adjusted leverage and cover history before FY2025. Severity: Low. Action: supply the fourth-quarter 2024 release or the 2024 non-GAAP reconciliation. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13

The issuer-adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 is derived from the twelve-month columns of the three 2026 releases and is not printed; the first and third releases give 1,583.8 and the second gives 1,583.9 in USD million, a rounding difference of 0.1. This restricts the FY2025 adjusted ratios to a derived figure. Severity: Low. Action: supply the fourth-quarter 2025 release. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31

Reported EBITDA is printed in no source, so the primary EBITDA figure for every period is constructed from income from operations plus depreciation and amortization; this restricts comparison with analyses that use another definition. Severity: Low. Action: none possible from the sources; the construction is shown in the income statement register. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

The repayment schedule of other finance obligations and finance leases is printed only at 2025-12-31, not at 2026-09-30, and these obligations of 161.904 USD million (3.48% of principal debt) are left out of the maturity ladder as a reconciling item; the 2025-12-31 schedule shows 13.915 USD million in 2026 and 160.615 USD million after 2030 of 183.891 USD million. This restricts the refinancing profile of that part of the debt. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the lease financing schedule at 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C101; calculation C49

The security and ranking of other finance obligations and finance leases are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and out of the secured and senior subtotals; this restricts the priority and recovery analysis for 3.48% of principal debt. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the lessor agreements and the credit documents. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C101

The names of the subsidiary guarantors are not printed and the assets and earnings of non-guarantor subsidiaries are not disclosed, so the structural subordination of the notes cannot be sized; this restricts the priority analysis. Severity: Medium. Action: supply Exhibit 21.1 and any guarantor financial information. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112

Carrying value net of issuance costs is not disclosed by instrument: the 10-K carrying amounts for the five note series equal their principal, and the unamortized discount and issuance costs of 43.679 USD million at 2025-12-31 and 39.740 USD million at 2026-09-30 are given only in aggregate, so the debt instrument register carries principal for each instrument and one financing cost adjustment row. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for leverage, which uses the carrying total. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C49

Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth in any source, so only total capital expenditure is carried and maintenance capital cover is not calculated. Severity: Low. Action: request the split from management. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

Cash flow and balance sheet cells printed as a dash are carried as missing, not zero: nine-month 2026 proceeds from long-term debt and other loans and payments of loan costs, the FY2024 deferred income tax asset, and the revolving facility principal at 2024-12-31; this restricts nothing material because every statement total foots. Severity: Low. Action: none needed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91

The debt note lists no subordinated instrument and states no subordinated amount, and no source states the minimum excess availability level at 2024-12-31, so the Subordinated Debt row and the FY2024 availability trigger cell are not supplied rather than zero. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the current analysis. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

The issuer reports one segment, and no revenue or profit by operating division is printed; the divisions were reduced from three to two in the second quarter of 2026. No segment schedule is stated and no segment sum is shown; sales by product category are printed but are not segments. Severity: Low. Action: none possible from the sources. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

The 10-Q prints the cash flow statement for nine months only; the third-quarter release prints three-month cash flows but no three-month cash interest paid, and the checked cash flow table carries annual and nine-month columns only. This restricts third-quarter cash flow analysis to the release, which is unaudited. Severity: Low. Action: build the discrete quarter from the first-half filing if needed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_bldr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

Reported-basis leverage and cover at 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 are not built in the checked tables; the quarterly path uses the issuer's printed twelve-month adjusted EBITDA and principal-basis net debt. This restricts the reported-basis trend to three points. Severity: Low. Action: build the first and second quarter periods if a quarterly reported-basis path is wanted. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3

Discretionary cash flow is not calculated because the method gives no definition and the issuer states that it pays no regular dividend; discretionary cash flow over total debt is not calculable. Severity: Low. Action: define the measure before use. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

The interest rate on other finance obligations and finance leases at 2026-09-30 is not printed; the issuer's interest reconciliation shows 6.3 USD million in the third quarter and 27.8 USD million in the nine months on 161.9 USD million outstanding, and interest on these obligations rose after purchase options were exercised, so the run-rate interest cost cannot be isolated; this restricts the interest forecast. Severity: Low. Action: request the financing obligation interest schedule. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13

No document dated after 2026-10-29 was supplied and the latest balance sheet is at 2026-09-30, 36 days before the as-of date; later financing, acquisition or buyback events cannot be ruled out. Severity: Low. Action: supply any current report filed since 2026-10-29. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder returns and acquisitions have outrun free cash flow since the start of 2025, and the gap was largely debt funded. Buybacks of USD 717.48 million and acquisitions of USD 1,240.01 million were 1.91x free cash flow of USD 1,024.91 million, while total debt rose USD 915.05 million. The mechanism is that returns and deals set in the strong cash generation of 2023 and 2024 continued as earnings fell, so the issuer's own net leverage measure reached 4.1x at 2026-09-30 against 2.3x a year earlier; bondholders therefore depend on board restraint, and the limits in the debt agreements could not be tested because the executed documents were not supplied. facts.text: The first-quarter 2026 buyback is the clearest creditor-adverse action, and it has not been repeated. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is cyclical and housing-start driven but not concentrated in customers. The ten largest customers were 14% of 2025 net sales and the largest 4%, and the four product categories each hold between 22.45% and 26.78% of sales. Demand follows single-family starts: in the third quarter core organic sales fell 6.2% in single-family, while multi-family rose 2.0%; production builders press prices, so margins and cash flow swing with the cycle, but no single customer default drives credit risk. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Builders FirstSource is a U.S. supplier and manufacturer of building materials, components and installation services for professional homebuilders, with about 575 locations in 43 states, one reportable segment and four product categories of similar size. The model supports cash-flow visibility through breadth and local density: the ten largest customers were 14% of 2025 net sales and the largest 4%. It weakens visibility through cyclicality, because orders follow housing starts and lumber prices; management calls the housing market underbuilt over the long term, which is Management Language and not evidence of near-term demand. Acquisitions of eight businesses in 2025 and four in 2026 have added scale at the cost of leverage and goodwill, and the notes' refinancing confidence rests on liquidity and a 2030-plus maturity profile rather than on demand visibility. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is cyclical, transactional and driven by single-family starts, repair and remodel and multi-family activity, with no contracted backlog or recurring element disclosed. In the third quarter of 2026 core organic single-family sales fell 6.2%, multi-family rose 2.0% and repair and remodel was up 0.3%, so volume is the main driver; commodity deflation reduced nine-month sales by 2.0% and acquisitions added 1.4%. Pricing power is limited because production builders press suppliers on price and costs are passed on only with a lag. The credit consequence is that revenue offers little visibility: sales declines flow quickly to earnings and cash, and the debt service capacity depends on cost and working-capital levers. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are largely fixed in the short run: selling, general and administrative expenses fell only 1.6% against a 7.0% fall in nine-month sales and rose to 25.8% of sales from 24.4%, while gross margin fell to 28.1% from 30.5%. Raw materials are lumber, OSB, plywood and other purchased products whose price swings are passed on with delay. Margins cannot be defended under volume pressure on the evidence: the fixed-cost base, wage inflation and fuel and insurance costs offset productivity savings of about USD 57 million. The implication is high operating leverage, measured at 5.80 times, so each point of lost sales costs several points of EBITDA. facts.label: Capital intensity and FCF conversion
facts.text: Capital intensity is moderate and flexible: purchases of property, plant and equipment were 2.39% of FY2025 sales, fell 42.65% in the nine months of 2026, and the 2026 outlook is USD 175 million to USD 225 million against USD 250 million to USD 300 million in the annual report. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high: the industry is fragmented and the annual report names national dealers, component manufacturers and home-centre chains expanding into the professional segment, so price competition limits margin recovery and weakens debt service capacity in a downturn. The threat of new entrants is moderate because barriers and costs of entry are described as low, although scale in manufacturing and procurement protects incumbents. The threat of substitutes arises from manufacturers selling directly to builders and builders integrating, which could erode distribution margin. Buyer power is high: production builders concentrate purchasing and press prices, though no customer exceeds 4% of sales. Supplier power is moderate: the largest suppliers are national producers and agreements are terminable on limited notice, but the company says it does not depend on any one supplier. facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Economic and trade factors are material and the rest are not primary credit drivers. Interest rates, mortgage affordability and consumer confidence set housing demand, and the composite forecast for 2026 shows total starts down 3.5% and single-family starts down 6.4%, which lowers volumes and so earnings and cash flow; tariffs on imported goods and commodity prices move input costs and margins. Regulation (building codes, trade policy, labour rules) adds cost but the sources do not show it changing probability of default on its own, and social and technological factors, such as skilled-labour scarcity and the new ERP system, matter mainly through cost and the recurring technology add-back. facts.label: SWOT analysis
facts.text: Strengths: liquidity of USD 1,514.11 million and no maturity before 2030; fixed-rate debt for most of the structure; diversified customers and products; a manufacturing and distribution footprint; no sponsor and restrictions on dividends. Weaknesses: reported leverage of 5.11x and interest cover of 3.18x; thin cash conversion; high operating leverage; reliance on management-defined add-backs. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: a housing recovery from an underbuilt base, lower interest rates, continued cost savings and deleveraging from free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it: a further fall in single-family starts, price deflation, renewed debt-funded buybacks or acquisitions, a shrinking borrowing base and the ERP programme's cost and disruption. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario is a further leg down in single-family starts and lumber and building-product prices, extending the decline already visible in 2026. Sales fall and, because EBITDA has fallen 5.80 times as fast as sales, reported EBITDA falls faster than sales and gross margin slips below the 27.82% of the third quarter while selling and administrative costs stay fixed. Free cash flow then depends on a working-capital release, which has occurred in FY2024 and FY2025 and in the downturns shown, but the borrowing base falls with receivables and inventory: in 2025 it fell 6.26% against a 7.38% fall in net sales, so availability shrinks roughly in step with sales. Leverage rises above 5.11x and cover falls below 3.18x, but liquidity is not at risk in this scenario because availability of USD 1,459.10 million is far above the USD 173.20 million level at which the fixed charge test applies, and the first debt maturities are in 2030. Management levers are capex (already down 42.65%), the paused buyback and acquisitions, and cost actions. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the exposure is a credit-quality deterioration through leverage and the notes' subordination, not a cash shortfall, unless buybacks resume on the revolver. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Builders FirstSource presents an adequate but weakening business profile supported by liquidity, a long fixed-rate maturity profile and diversified customers, but credit quality is constrained by falling margins, thin cash conversion and reported leverage above 5x. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because free cash flow was 28.74% of EBITDA over the last twelve months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings stabilising before the 2030 maturities and on the board holding back buybacks. The primary downside path is a further fall in single-family volumes and prices that cuts EBITDA faster than sales and lifts leverage while the secured revolver ranks ahead of the notes. Further analysis would require peer data, the covenant documents and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: earnings erosion in the single-family housing cycle, amplified by fixed costs and a policy that has been partly debt funded. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

## Request

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and earnings releases support the financial, liquidity and fundamental-credit work this snapshot needs, but they cannot support firm conclusions on governance, ownership, ratings or legal protections, so creditors should treat those areas as unverified.

The annual report and the three quarterly reports each print full statements, a debt note and a borrowing-base table, and the printed debt, borrowing-base and quarterly totals reproduce from their parts within rounding. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA appears only in the earnings releases, and its 2025 full-year figure has to be derived rather than read. Board, ownership and executive pay sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, no credit rating appears anywhere, and the credit agreement and indentures are known only through the annual report's summaries. Nothing dated after the third-quarter release is available.

## Request

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditor protection has weakened: total debt was 5.11x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 3.22x at FY2025, because earnings fell while debt grew, and EBITDA covered cash interest only 3.18x.
Basis: calculation C61; calculation C55; calculation C63

The issuer's own adjusted measure looks milder, at 4.1x net debt to adjusted EBITDA, because its adjusted EBITDA is USD 224.70 million above reported EBITDA, mostly technology implementation and stock compensation add-backs. No note or revolver matures before 2030 and liquidity is USD 1,514.11 million, so the exposure is further earnings erosion rather than a near-term refinancing.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C78; calculation C45; calculation C48
### Key findings

Debt rose while earnings fell. Total debt at carrying value was USD 4,619.16 million at 2026-09-30, USD 177.80 million above FY2025, after the revolving facility was drawn for USD 197.00 million. Last-twelve-month reported EBITDA was USD 904.40 million, 34.35% below the USD 1,377.71 million of FY2025, so net debt of USD 4,564.15 million stands at 5.05x. The earnings fall, not new borrowing, explains most of the rise: had EBITDA stayed at the FY2025 level, total debt would be 3.35x EBITDA.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C91; calculation C9; calculation C94; calculation C37; calculation C92

The fall is operational. Nine-month 2026 net sales were 7.01% lower than a year earlier, gross margin fell from 30.54% to 28.06% of sales and income from operations dropped from USD 724.50 million to USD 244.11 million, because selling and administrative costs fell only 1.57% while sales and commodity prices fell. The issuer attributes the decline to lower housing starts: core organic sales fell 6.40% and commodity deflation took 2.00%, partly offset by acquisitions. The quarterly sales decline narrowed from 10.13% in the first quarter to 2.21% in the third, but third-quarter gross margin of 27.82% was the lowest of the three quarters of 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C93; calculation C70; calculation C74; calculation C75

The gap between the two leverage views is the add-backs. Technology implementation expense is USD 149.00 million of the USD 224.70 million by which adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA, or 13.20% of adjusted EBITDA, and it rose from USD 93.50 million in the first nine months of 2025 to USD 106.90 million in 2026; in this analyst's judgement a cost that recurs and grows is not a one-off. Total debt over adjusted EBITDA is 4.09x and net debt over adjusted EBITDA 4.04x, so last-twelve-month leverage runs from 4.04x to 5.11x depending on the definitions, and the issuer's headline of 4.1x uses principal debt.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C78; calculation C95; calculation C64; calculation C65; calculation C39

Interest cover has thinned sharply. Cash interest paid was USD 284.75 million over the last twelve months, up from USD 260.52 million in FY2025 and USD 188.45 million in FY2024, while reported EBITDA cover fell from 11.45x to 5.29x to 3.18x, or 3.97x on adjusted EBITDA. The interest bill is structural: the 6.75% 2035 notes issued in May 2025 added USD 750.00 million of debt, and the issuer also cites interest on other finance obligations after purchase options were exercised.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C54; calculation C57; calculation C63; calculation C66; calculation C11

Cash conversion has fallen sharply. Operating cash flow was USD 302.03 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 1,021.09 million a year earlier, as lower earnings met a working-capital build in receivables and inventories that higher payables only partly offset. Free cash flow on the issuer's definition was USD 150.88 million, 21.83% of nine-month reported EBITDA against 63.44% for FY2025. Buybacks of USD 303.52 million, almost all in the first quarter, were 2.01x free cash flow, and acquisitions took USD 116.68 million, so the revolver draw financed shareholder returns and deals, not operations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-03-31_bldr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C25; calculation C96; calculation C4

Customer deposits are a small float and trade credit a large one. Contract liabilities, which hold customer advances and deposits and are recognised as revenue within the year, were USD 181.88 million at 2026-09-30, against USD 168.44 million at FY2025, so they unwind into sales rather than into a cash claim. Accounts payable rose USD 185.48 million to USD 900.19 million and supplied USD 178.06 million of nine-month operating cash flow; that support would reverse, and liquidity would fall, if suppliers shortened terms or purchases slowed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C100

Liquidity is adequate but has narrowed. Cash of USD 55.01 million and net borrowing availability of USD 1,459.10 million give USD 1,514.11 million, down from USD 1,709.05 million at FY2025 and USD 1,784.62 million at FY2024. Availability is capped by a borrowing base of USD 1,731.70 million, not the USD 2,200.00 million of commitments, which leaves USD 468.30 million unusable. The fixed charge coverage test of 1.00x applies only if availability falls below USD 173.20 million; that is a trigger level, not a measure of covenant headroom.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation C41; calculation C43; calculation C45; calculation C47; calculation C97

The debt is long-dated and mostly fixed rate, which limits refinancing risk. Five senior unsecured note series total USD 4,300.00 million, maturing between 2030 and 2035; the only debt stated to be secured is the revolving facility, drawn for USD 197.00 million and due 2030-05-20. No note or revolver principal falls due before 2030; USD 747.00 million falls due in 2030, followed by USD 2,000.00 million in 2032. The notes rank behind the secured revolver and behind the non-guarantor subsidiaries, whose size is not disclosed, and USD 161.17 million of other finance obligations on leased properties sit in debt with no stated ranking.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; calculation C48; calculation C50
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that the structure buys time. No note or revolver matures before 2030, the notes are fixed rate, liquidity is USD 1,514.11 million and free cash flow remains positive. The issuer guides full-year free cash flow of USD 400.00 million to USD 450.00 million, which would imply USD 249.13 million to USD 299.13 million in the fourth quarter; that arithmetic is the analyst's, not the issuer's. Sales declines have also narrowed, with core organic sales down 3.90% in the third quarter against 8.30% in the first.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-03-31_bldr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C98; calculation C45

The view would improve if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA reaches the range implied by the issuer's full-year outlook of USD 1,075.00 million to USD 1,125.00 million, which is USD 220.80 million to USD 270.80 million against USD 274.90 million derived for the fourth quarter of 2025, and if free cash flow repays revolver borrowings. It would worsen if availability falls toward the USD 173.20 million trigger, if buybacks or acquisitions are again funded on the revolver, or if gross margin falls below the third-quarter level.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C99; calculation C31
### Limitations

The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so the primary leverage and cover figures use a constructed measure, income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, and will differ from any analysis that defines EBITDA differently.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C2; calculation C9

Adjusted EBITDA exists only in the issuer's releases and is issuer-defined; the FY2025 figure is derived and the FY2024 figure is not supplied, so adjusted leverage before the first quarter of 2026 rests on one derived point.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C29; calculation C31
The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is built from each instrument's stated maturity year, and the repayment schedule of USD 161.17 million of other finance obligations is printed only at 2025-12-31.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C48; calculation C49

Guarantor names, the assets and earnings of non-guarantor subsidiaries, the security over other finance obligations and the executed credit documents are not available, so structural and legal priority are described and not sized.

The statement tables cover FY2024, FY2025 and the nine-month periods; reported-basis leverage at the first and second quarter-ends is not built, and the quarterly trend relies on the issuer's printed twelve-month adjusted figures on a principal basis.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3
No document dated after 2026-10-29 was supplied and the balance sheet is at 2026-09-30, 36 days before the as-of date, so later financing events cannot be ruled out.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1

## Gaps
Each gap states what is missing, what it restricts, its severity and the action that would close it.

The issuer-adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 is printed in no supplied source, so the six adjusted ratio rows for FY2024 and the FY2024 adjusted EBITDA cell are not supplied; this restricts adjusted leverage and cover history before FY2025. Severity: Low. Action: supply the fourth-quarter 2024 release or the 2024 non-GAAP reconciliation.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13

The issuer-adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 is derived from the twelve-month columns of the three 2026 releases and is not printed; the first and third releases give 1,583.8 and the second gives 1,583.9 in USD million, a rounding difference of 0.1. This restricts the FY2025 adjusted ratios to a derived figure. Severity: Low. Action: supply the fourth-quarter 2025 release.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31

Reported EBITDA is printed in no source, so the primary EBITDA figure for every period is constructed from income from operations plus depreciation and amortization; this restricts comparison with analyses that use another definition. Severity: Low. Action: none possible from the sources; the construction is shown in the income statement register.

The repayment schedule of other finance obligations and finance leases is printed only at 2025-12-31, not at 2026-09-30, and these obligations of 161.904 USD million (3.48% of principal debt) are left out of the maturity ladder as a reconciling item; the 2025-12-31 schedule shows 13.915 USD million in 2026 and 160.615 USD million after 2030 of 183.891 USD million. This restricts the refinancing profile of that part of the debt. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the lease financing schedule at 2026-09-30.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C101; calculation C49

The security and ranking of other finance obligations and finance leases are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and out of the secured and senior subtotals; this restricts the priority and recovery analysis for 3.48% of principal debt. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the lessor agreements and the credit documents.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C101

Severity: Medium. Action: supply Exhibit 21.1 and any guarantor financial information.

Carrying value net of issuance costs is not disclosed by instrument: the 10-K carrying amounts for the five note series equal their principal, and the unamortized discount and issuance costs of 43.679 USD million at 2025-12-31 and 39.740 USD million at 2026-09-30 are given only in aggregate, so the debt instrument register carries principal for each instrument and one financing cost adjustment row. # Business and governance for Builders FirstSource, Inc. (bldr), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Business and governance for Builders FirstSource, Inc. (bldr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: transaction and financing history, business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, sponsor behaviour and capital allocation, from the seven supplied filings and releases and the source readiness answer.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance risk is medium and comes from capital allocation, not ownership: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, but debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions raised leverage while earnings fell.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C5; calculation C6

Debt agreements restrict dividends, cash buybacks stopped after the first quarter of 2026 and reporting is audited and regular, which limits extraction risk. Board, ownership and pay detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so control and independence are not established.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 106–108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

No sponsor or controlling owner is identified, so the creditor risk is board policy, not an owner's extraction. The common stock is listed on the NYSE and NYSE Texas with 62 stockholders of record, the company pays no dividends and its debt agreements restrict dividends and buybacks. Beneficial ownership sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so a large holder cannot be ruled out. With no sponsor there are no monitoring fees or fund-life pressure to assess; the risk is a policy that a board can change quickly.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 106–108; Source readiness (CP-0)

Shareholder returns and acquisitions have outrun free cash flow since the start of 2025, and the gap was largely debt funded. Buybacks of USD 717.48 million and acquisitions of USD 1,240.01 million were 1.91x free cash flow of USD 1,024.91 million, while total debt rose USD 915.05 million. The mechanism is that returns and deals set in the strong cash generation of 2023 and 2024 continued as earnings fell, so the issuer's own net leverage measure reached 4.1x at 2026-09-30 against 2.3x a year earlier; bondholders therefore depend on board restraint, and the limits in the debt agreements could not be tested because the executed documents were not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

The first-quarter 2026 buyback is the clearest creditor-adverse action, and it has not been repeated. The company repurchased USD 302.90 million of stock at an average of USD 92.25 a share and drew a net USD 200.00 million on the revolving facility while adjusted EBITDA was falling and the issuer's net leverage measure stood at 3.2x against 2.0x a year earlier. No shares were bought under the programme in the second or third quarter, although the board authorised up to USD 500.00 million on 2026-04-29; the pause is supportive, and a repurchase funded on the revolver would be the trigger to watch.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-30_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-03-31_bldr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C7

Acquisitions are a repeated, mostly cash-funded growth route that raises leverage in a downturn, but 2026 activity is far smaller. In 2025 the company completed eight acquisitions using USD 1,123.33 million of cash net of cash acquired, funded by cash and revolver borrowings and then termed out with the USD 750.00 million notes of May 2025; in the first nine months of 2026 it completed four acquisitions for about USD 129.30 million. The earnings contribution and pro forma leverage of these deals are not disclosed because the company calls them immaterial, so their effect on creditors cannot be separated from the organic decline.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 86–87; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation C3

Disclosure is regular and audited, but the largest EBITDA adjustment is management-defined and recurring. The auditor gives an unqualified opinion on the statements and on internal control, and each release reconciles its non-GAAP measures; however technology implementation expense of USD 149.00 million over the last twelve months is added back while the new ERP system is rolled out in phases over several years, so more such add-backs should be expected. Adjusted and reported EBITDA should therefore be read side by side.

The business is cyclical and housing-start driven but not concentrated in customers. The ten largest customers were 14% of 2025 net sales and the largest 4%, and the four product categories each hold between 22.45% and 26.78% of sales. Demand follows single-family starts: in the third quarter core organic sales fell 6.2% in single-family, while multi-family rose 2.0%; production builders press prices, so margins and cash flow swing with the cycle, but no single customer default drives credit risk.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C9; calculation C11

Management is adapting capacity and cost to the downturn. The location count fell by about ten between the annual report and the third-quarter release, the three operating divisions were merged into two in the second quarter of 2026, productivity savings reached about USD 57.00 million in the first nine months, and purchases of property, plant and equipment fell 42.65% year on year; this gives some flexibility, though the cost base remains largely fixed in the near term.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C8
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a lower risk level is that the company has no sponsor, pays no dividend, is bound by restrictions on dividends and buybacks and has made no cash buybacks since the first quarter of 2026, while holding liquidity of USD 1,514.11 million and having no note or revolver maturity before 2030. The 2026 acquisition spend is also far below that of 2025. The view would move to low if the proxy statement shows an independent board and no large controlling holder, leverage falls through earnings recovery or debt repayment, and the buyback authorisation lapses unused.

The view would move to high if buybacks resume funded by the revolver while availability falls, if new debt is raised to fund distributions, or if an amendment weakens the restricted-payment limits; none of these is documented in the sources read.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so board independence, ownership concentration, executive pay and related-party dealings are not established; each could move the medium governance view in either direction.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 106–108; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares, invest or incur debt is not assessed; the view rests on documented behaviour and not on legal capacity.

- The earnings contribution and pro forma EBITDA of acquisitions are not disclosed, so the leverage effect of deal spending cannot be separated from the organic decline and the acquisition finding is directional only.

- Executive incentive design is known only for performance share units, which reward return on invested capital and relative shareholder return, so whether pay encourages leverage reduction or further buybacks is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15
- Customer contract terms and pricing power are not disclosed beyond the ten-customer share and the five largest named customers, so pricing pressure is described and not measured.

### Overall governance view

Overall, Builders FirstSource presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behavior is debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions while earnings fell, which matters because the cash left the business just as leverage needed to fall and implies a thinner cushion for creditors. Countervailing evidence is that no sponsor exists, dividends are restricted, cash buybacks paused after the first quarter of 2026 and liquidity is adequate. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the executed credit documents. Governance review completed with limitations. Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. Key gaps: board and ownership detail, pay design and covenant capacity.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No sponsor, buy-out or change-of-control transaction is described in the sources read; the company is publicly listed and its financing and capital allocation events are the transactions that matter to creditors.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; Source readiness (CP-0)

Debt issued in the period covered is limited to two note offerings: the USD 1.0 billion 6.375% notes due 2034 on 2024-02-29, whose proceeds repaid revolver borrowings and funded general corporate purposes, and the USD 750.0 million 6.75% notes due 2035 on 2025-05-08, whose proceeds repaid revolver borrowings. The revolving facility was amended on 2025-05-20, raising commitments from USD 1.8 billion to USD 2.2 billion and extending maturity to 2030-05-20. No new debt was issued in 2026 to the third quarter, and the revolver was drawn for USD 197.0 million at 2026-09-30 after funding buybacks and acquisitions.

Acquisitions were eight in 2025 for about USD 1.1 billion net of cash acquired and four in the first nine months of 2026 for about USD 129.3 million, funded with cash and revolver borrowings; pro forma figures are not presented because the company calls them immaterial. A strategic investment in Digs was announced on 2026-08-25, and the board authorised repurchases of up to USD 500.0 million on 2026-04-29, of which none was used in the second or third quarter.

# Fundamental credit for Builders FirstSource, Inc. (bldr), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Fundamental credit for Builders FirstSource, Inc. (bldr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, financial profile, outlook, downside scenario, materiality ranking and monitoring triggers, drawing on the seven supplied filings and releases and the three earlier module answers.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit has weakened sharply but is not distressed: reported leverage reached 5.11x and interest cover fell to 3.18x as earnings fell, yet USD 1,514.11 million of liquidity and no note or revolver maturity before 2030 give creditors time.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

The weakest points are margin and cash conversion in a single-family housing downturn and a shareholder policy that has been partly debt funded; the strongest are liquidity, long-dated fixed-rate debt and a diversified customer base. The primary downside path is a further fall in single-family volumes and prices that cuts earnings faster than sales, which would push leverage higher well before it threatens liquidity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5
### Key findings

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main credit support, and they remove near-term refinancing risk. Cash of USD 55.01 million and net borrowing availability of USD 1,459.10 million sit under a borrowing base of USD 1,731.70 million, and the USD 4,300.00 million of senior unsecured notes are 92.30% of principal and fixed rate. The first principal due is USD 550.00 million in March 2030, so note and revolver debt service before then is interest only; the floating-rate revolver is only 4.23% of principal.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C12; calculation C13

Earnings erosion is the weakest dimension: margins have roughly halved since FY2024. Reported EBITDA margin fell from 13.15% to 9.07% and then 6.30% over the last twelve months, and last-twelve-month reported EBITDA of USD 904.40 million is 34.35% below FY2025. The mechanism is fixed cost: nine-month EBITDA fell 5.80x as fast as net sales, so a small further sales decline compounds into a large EBITDA decline and a higher leverage ratio.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C5

Cash conversion has fallen sharply, so deleveraging cannot yet rely on free cash flow. Free cash flow was 28.74% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months against 63.44% in FY2025, and a nine-month working-capital outflow of USD 198.77 million took 65.81% of operating cash flow. Purchases of property, plant and equipment fell 42.65% and the issuer guides full-year free cash flow of USD 400.00 million to USD 450.00 million, which would imply USD 249.13 million to USD 299.13 million in the fourth quarter on the analyst's arithmetic as seasonal working capital releases.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C15; calculation C1

Leverage is high on the reported basis and the issuer's headline understates it. Total debt was 5.11x reported EBITDA, 4.09x adjusted EBITDA, and 3.22x at FY2025; the issuer's own net measure is 4.1x against 2.3x a year earlier. Cash interest paid of USD 284.75 million over the last twelve months is 51.10% above FY2024, so EBITDA covers it only 3.18x (3.97x on adjusted EBITDA).
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13

Financial policy is the main discretionary risk, and the pause since the first quarter of 2026 is the best mitigant. Buybacks and acquisitions since the start of 2025 were 1.91x free cash flow and total debt rose USD 915.05 million, while no shares were bought under the programme in the second or third quarter even though USD 500.00 million of authority remains; governance risk is medium, with board, ownership and pay detail not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

Structure matters for loss given default: the notes sit behind a secured revolver that can be drawn up to the borrowing base. The revolver is drawn for USD 197.00 million but its secured claim could rise towards USD 1,731.70 million, the notes are guaranteed by unnamed subsidiaries and are structurally behind non-guarantors, and USD 161.17 million of other finance obligations carry no stated ranking. Cumulative leverage through the notes is 4.97x; sizing recovery is left to the priority and recovery work.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

The issuer's outlook points to flat-to-slightly-lower leverage by year-end, not a sharp recovery. If the outlook is met and nothing is spent on buybacks or acquisitions in the fourth quarter, the issuer's net leverage measure would be about 3.83x to 4.05x on the analyst's arithmetic, against 4.1x now, and guided adjusted EBITDA over guided interest expense would be 3.58x to 3.88x; the cycle trough is not yet shown.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C3; calculation C4
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weakening view is that the decline is narrowing and the market is not pricing distress. Net sales fell 10.13% in the first quarter, 8.77% in the second and 2.21% in the third, the issuer's adjusted EBITDA decline eased from 42.1% to 28.3%, and the five note series were valued at 88.25% to 96.38% of principal in the third-quarter filing, below the 95.12% to 104.75% range at year-end but not at distressed levels (the 5.00% 2030 notes moved least). The view would improve if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA reaches the USD 220.80 million to USD 270.80 million the outlook implies and free cash flow repays revolver borrowings.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C2; calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C9

It would worsen if single-family core organic sales fall by more than the 6.2% of the third quarter, if gross margin falls below the 27.82% of that quarter, if buybacks resume on the revolver, or if availability moves towards the USD 173.20 million level at which the fixed charge test applies.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27
### Limitations

- No peer financials or agency ratings were supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers in building products and the strength assessments rest on issuer evidence alone.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The notes' fair values are balance-sheet-date disclosures from observable prices, not dated quotes supplied for this run, so market access and the cost of refinancing are inferred from filings and not tested against live levels.
- The year-end leverage range depends on the issuer's own outlook and on no fourth-quarter buybacks or acquisitions, so it changes with either; it is an illustration, not a forecast.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C3

- The fixed charge ratio definition and covenant baskets were not supplied, so the downside scenario shows where the availability test applies but cannot show a coverage result or any restricted-payment capacity.
- Earnings are not split by division, customer or region, so the margin decline is traced to company-wide volume, price and fixed-cost effects only.

### Company description

Builders FirstSource is a U.S. supplier and manufacturer of building materials, components and installation services for professional homebuilders, with about 575 locations in 43 states, one reportable segment and four product categories of similar size. The model supports cash-flow visibility through breadth and local density: the ten largest customers were 14% of 2025 net sales and the largest 4%. It weakens visibility through cyclicality, because orders follow housing starts and lumber prices; management calls the housing market underbuilt over the long term, which is Management Language and not evidence of near-term demand. Acquisitions of eight businesses in 2025 and four in 2026 have added scale at the cost of leverage and goodwill, and the notes' refinancing confidence rests on liquidity and a 2030-plus maturity profile rather than on demand visibility.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59
### Ownership and group structure

The company is publicly held and listed on the NYSE and NYSE Texas, with no sponsor or controlling holder identified in the sources read; beneficial ownership, board independence and pay sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. The group is one consolidated entity with unnamed subsidiary guarantors of the revolver and notes, so notes are structurally behind the liabilities of any non-guarantor subsidiary whose size is not disclosed. Debt agreements restrict dividends and buybacks, and the company pays no dividend. Financial policy has favoured buybacks and acquisitions funded partly by debt, which lifts leverage and shows a tolerance for higher leverage; the governance review rates the overall risk medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical, transactional and driven by single-family starts, repair and remodel and multi-family activity, with no contracted backlog or recurring element disclosed. In the third quarter of 2026 core organic single-family sales fell 6.2%, multi-family rose 2.0% and repair and remodel was up 0.3%, so volume is the main driver; commodity deflation reduced nine-month sales by 2.0% and acquisitions added 1.4%. Pricing power is limited because production builders press suppliers on price and costs are passed on only with a lag. The credit consequence is that revenue offers little visibility: sales declines flow quickly to earnings and cash, and the debt service capacity depends on cost and working-capital levers.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are largely fixed in the short run: selling, general and administrative expenses fell only 1.6% against a 7.0% fall in nine-month sales and rose to 25.8% of sales from 24.4%, while gross margin fell to 28.1% from 30.5%. Raw materials are lumber, OSB, plywood and other purchased products whose price swings are passed on with delay. Margins cannot be defended under volume pressure on the evidence: the fixed-cost base, wage inflation and fuel and insurance costs offset productivity savings of about USD 57 million. The implication is high operating leverage, measured at 5.80 times, so each point of lost sales costs several points of EBITDA.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C5
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital intensity is moderate and flexible: purchases of property, plant and equipment were 2.39% of FY2025 sales, fell 42.65% in the nine months of 2026, and the 2026 outlook is USD 175 million to USD 225 million against USD 250 million to USD 300 million in the annual report. Working capital is the swing factor: it released cash in FY2024 and FY2025 but absorbed USD 198.77 million in nine months 2026, and the first half is seasonally heavy. Technology implementation and acquisition spend add cash costs that are added back in adjusted EBITDA. EBITDA converted to free cash flow at 69.82% in FY2024 and 63.44% in FY2025 but only 28.74% over the last twelve months, so free cash flow available for debt service and deleveraging is currently thin and depends on a working-capital release.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is high: the industry is fragmented and the annual report names national dealers, component manufacturers and home-centre chains expanding into the professional segment, so price competition limits margin recovery and weakens debt service capacity in a downturn. The threat of new entrants is moderate because barriers and costs of entry are described as low, although scale in manufacturing and procurement protects incumbents. The threat of substitutes arises from manufacturers selling directly to builders and builders integrating, which could erode distribution margin. Buyer power is high: production builders concentrate purchasing and press prices, though no customer exceeds 4% of sales. Supplier power is moderate: the largest suppliers are national producers and agreements are terminable on limited notice, but the company says it does not depend on any one supplier.
### PEST analysis

Economic and trade factors are material and the rest are not primary credit drivers. Interest rates, mortgage affordability and consumer confidence set housing demand, and the composite forecast for 2026 shows total starts down 3.5% and single-family starts down 6.4%, which lowers volumes and so earnings and cash flow; tariffs on imported goods and commodity prices move input costs and margins. Regulation (building codes, trade policy, labour rules) adds cost but the sources do not show it changing probability of default on its own, and social and technological factors, such as skilled-labour scarcity and the new ERP system, matter mainly through cost and the recurring technology add-back.
### SWOT analysis

Strengths: liquidity of USD 1,514.11 million and no maturity before 2030; fixed-rate debt for most of the structure; diversified customers and products; a manufacturing and distribution footprint; no sponsor and restrictions on dividends. Weaknesses: reported leverage of 5.11x and interest cover of 3.18x; thin cash conversion; high operating leverage; reliance on management-defined add-backs. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: a housing recovery from an underbuilt base, lower interest rates, continued cost savings and deleveraging from free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it: a further fall in single-family starts, price deflation, renewed debt-funded buybacks or acquisitions, a shrinking borrowing base and the ERP programme's cost and disruption.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position is strong on size, with USD 15,190.64 million of FY2025 net sales and wide market coverage, although market share is not established. Competitive advantage is average: local density and manufacturing breadth are real but entry barriers are low. Business diversification is average: customers and products are diversified but demand is concentrated in U.S. residential construction. Cost and capex flexibility is average: costs are largely fixed but capex, buybacks and acquisitions can be cut. Margin stability is weak: reported EBITDA margin fell from 13.15% to 6.30%. Free cash flow stability is weak: conversion fell to 28.74%. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: no maturity before 2030 and market access in May 2025, offset by rising leverage and notes valued below par. Liquidity position is strong at USD 1,514.11 million. Financial policy and governance is average: no sponsor and restricted dividends against debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions. The main supports are liquidity, maturities and diversification; the constraints are earnings, cash conversion and policy; the trend is deteriorating; the key missing data are peer comparisons, covenant terms and the proxy statement.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Short term (12 to 24 months): the issuer expects 2026 net sales of USD 14.2 billion to USD 14.6 billion, adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,075 million to USD 1,125 million and free cash flow of USD 400 million to USD 450 million, on assumptions of lower single-family and multi-family starts and repair and remodel down 1%; that points to a stabilising level of earnings and leverage near 4x on the issuer's measure, so deleveraging relies on free cash flow and not on earnings growth. Medium term (three to five years): the 2030 maturities of USD 747.00 million, the revolver and the 5.00% notes, are the refinancing test. Sector tailwinds are an underbuilt housing stock and demographics (Management Language); sector headwinds are affordability, interest rates, tariffs and labour. Company tailwinds are productivity savings, lower capex and the 2025 financing; company headwinds are fixed costs, add-backs and the ERP programme.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario is a further leg down in single-family starts and lumber and building-product prices, extending the decline already visible in 2026. Sales fall and, because EBITDA has fallen 5.80 times as fast as sales, reported EBITDA falls faster than sales and gross margin slips below the 27.82% of the third quarter while selling and administrative costs stay fixed. Free cash flow then depends on a working-capital release, which has occurred in FY2024 and FY2025 and in the downturns shown, but the borrowing base falls with receivables and inventory: in 2025 it fell 6.26% against a 7.38% fall in net sales, so availability shrinks roughly in step with sales. Leverage rises above 5.11x and cover falls below 3.18x, but liquidity is not at risk in this scenario because availability of USD 1,459.10 million is far above the USD 173.20 million level at which the fixed charge test applies, and the first debt maturities are in 2030. Management levers are capex (already down 42.65%), the paused buyback and acquisitions, and cost actions. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the exposure is a credit-quality deterioration through leverage and the notes' subordination, not a cash shortfall, unless buybacks resume on the revolver.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C5; calculation C6

### Overall credit view

Overall, Builders FirstSource presents an adequate but weakening business profile supported by liquidity, a long fixed-rate maturity profile and diversified customers, but credit quality is constrained by falling margins, thin cash conversion and reported leverage above 5x. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because free cash flow was 28.74% of EBITDA over the last twelve months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings stabilising before the 2030 maturities and on the board holding back buybacks. The primary downside path is a further fall in single-family volumes and prices that cuts EBITDA faster than sales and lifts leverage while the secured revolver ranks ahead of the notes. Further analysis would require peer data, the covenant documents and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: earnings erosion in the single-family housing cycle, amplified by fixed costs and a policy that has been partly debt funded.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: liquidity and long-dated, fixed-rate debt. Liquidity of USD 1,514.11 million with no note or revolver maturity before 2030 means debt service is interest only for several years, which keeps near-term default risk low.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

Strength: diversified customers and products. The ten largest customers were 14% of net sales and no product category exceeds 26.78%, so a single customer or product shock is unlikely to threaten debt service.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength: flexibility in cash use. Capex fell 42.65% in the nine months, cash buybacks paused after the first quarter and productivity savings reached about USD 57 million, which preserves liquidity while earnings fall.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bldr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_bldr-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3
Strength: no sponsor and restricted dividends. With no sponsor to extract fees or dividends, leakage is limited to buybacks and acquisitions the board chooses.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bldr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53
Weakness: earnings erosion and high reported leverage. EBITDA is 34.35% below FY2025 and total debt is 5.11x reported EBITDA, so the cushion for noteholders has thinned.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
Weakness: operating leverage in a cyclical single-family business. EBITDA fell 5.80 times as fast as sales, so a further volume decline raises leverage quickly.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5
Weakness: cash conversion. Free cash flow is 28.74% of EBITDA over twelve months and working capital absorbed 65.81% of nine-month operating cash flow, so deleveraging is slow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C15

Weakness: financial policy and structure. Buybacks and acquisitions exceeded free cash flow by 1.91 times since the start of 2025 and the notes rank behind a secured revolver and non-guarantors, which weakens recovery prospects.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)
